mainTopic: רבא's case of a שעיר המשתלח that is מחוסר זמן. The dispute between רב and רבי יוחנן over whether בעלי חיים נדחין, including the reading of 'בהם' and רב's reliance on רבי יוסי's rule of מצוה בראשון.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question: how could the שעיר המשתלח (the goat sent to עזאזל) ever be מחוסר זמן? רבא answers that the goat's mother was slaughtered on יום הכיפורים to save a sick person, so the איסור of אותו ואת בנו blocks the goat that day. The גמרא objects that this goat is pushed off a cliff, not slaughtered. It answers with a teaching from ארץ ישראל that the push off the cliff counts as this goat's שחיטה. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's case where one goat died and a new pair was brought. רב says the leftover goat of the first pair is offered, and רבי יוחנן says it grazes. Their argument is whether בעלי חיים נדחין, meaning whether a live animal that was pushed off stays pushed off forever. רב's source is a בעל מום עובר, an animal with a temporary blemish. The two sides then argue over how to read the word 'בהם' in the פסוק, which also connects to a משנה about mixed limbs. Finally, רבא explains that רב gives the first goat priority because he follows רבי יוסי's rule of מצוה בראשון, which comes from the case of a lost קרבן פסח.

steps.title: רבא's case of a scapegoat that is lacking time
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains how the שעיר המשתלח could be מחוסר זמן: its mother was slaughtered that same day, on יום הכיפורים, to feed a dangerously ill person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: For example, the seller had a sick person in his house, and he slaughtered the goat's mother on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer to the earlier question: how could the goat for עזאזל ever be 'not yet allowed' (מחוסר זמן)?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah forbids killing a mother animal and its young on the same day (אותו ואת בנו). If the mother was slaughtered on יום הכיפורים to save a sick person's life, then the young goat cannot be 'slaughtered' that day. So even a grown goat can be מחוסר זמן.

keyTerms.meaning: A sick person (here, one in danger, so slaughtering on יום הכיפורים is allowed)
'Lacking time': an animal not yet allowed to be used, because of timing
The איסור against slaughtering a mother animal and its young on the same day

steps.confusionAlert: The 'sick person' detail is not just color. It explains why anyone would slaughter on יום הכיפורים at all. Slaughtering is forbidden work on יום הכיפורים, but saving a life (פיקוח נפש) overrides that ban.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ חוֹלֶה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ,
phrases.english: For example, where he had a sick person in his house,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the seller of the goats.

phrases.english: and he slaughtered its mother on Yom Kippur.
phrases.notes: Now the young goat falls under the rule of mother-and-young on the same day.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה לוֹ חוֹלֶה בְּתוֹךְ בֵּיתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another answer to the earlier question (on the previous amud) of how the שעיר המשתלח could be מחוסר זמן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A realistic case where the שעיר המשתלח is מחוסר זמן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Its mother was slaughtered on יום הכיפורים for a sick person, so אותו ואת בנו makes the goat unusable that day.

steps.title: Challenge: pushing off a cliff is not slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the איסור of אותו ואת בנו only covers שחיטה, and the שעיר המשתלח is pushed off a cliff, not slaughtered.
steps.simpleTranslation: In a case like this, is it really forbidden? The Torah said 'do not slaughter,' and this is not slaughtering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבא's case. It says the mother-and-young rule should not apply to this goat at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'לא תשחטו', 'do not slaughter.' The goat for עזאזל is never slaughtered. It is pushed off a cliff. So it seems the goat is not blocked, and רבא's case fails.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Merciful One,' meaning the Torah / ה׳

phrases.english: And in a case like this, is it forbidden?
The Merciful One said: 'You shall not slaughter,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא כ״ב:כ״ח, about a mother and its young.

phrases.english: but this is not slaughter!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's case from step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that אותו ואת בנו makes the שעיר המשתלח מחוסר זמן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids only שחיטה. Pushing off a cliff is not שחיטה, so the איסור should not apply.

steps.title: Answer: in ארץ ישראל they say the cliff counts as slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a teaching from ארץ ישראל: for the שעיר המשתלח, pushing it off the cliff is its שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say in the West (ארץ ישראל): pushing it off the cliff is its slaughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבא by quoting a teaching from ארץ ישראל. That teaching treats the push off the cliff as this goat's form of שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The push off the cliff is the official way this goat's מצוה ends, so it takes the place of שחיטה. That means 'לא תשחטו' does apply to it. רבא's case stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's case works: the goat's mother was slaughtered that day, and the cliff push counts as the goat's 'slaughter.' So the שעיר המשתלח can be מחוסר זמן.

phrases.english: But they say in the West:
pushing it off the cliff, that is its slaughter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the key term: the cliff push counts as שחיטה for this goat.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only real knife slaughter counts, so אותו ואת בנו would not apply.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the שעיר המשתלח, the push off the cliff is its שחיטה, so the איסור applies.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: if the goat for God died
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new section by quoting the משנה. If one goat died after the גורל and a new pair was brought, the new goat chosen by lot takes its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] If the goat 'for God' died, the one on which [that lot] came up [takes its place], etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the dispute that comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה's case, one of the two goats died after the lottery, so a new pair was brought and a new lottery drawn. The new goat replaces the dead one. That leaves one extra goat, either from the old pair or the new pair. The next steps argue over which extra goat is used and which one grazes.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat 'for God' (offered as a קרבן)
Etc.: the rest of the משנה line

phrases.english: If the one for God died,
this one, on which [the lot] came up, etc.
phrases.notes: The new goat that got the same lot takes the dead goat's place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם שֶׁל שֵׁם מֵת, זֶה שֶׁעָלָה עָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic; not connected to רבא's discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A goat that died after the lottery is replaced by the matching goat from a new lottery.

steps.title: רב: the leftover of the first pair is offered
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that the surviving goat from the first pair is offered, and the extra goat from the second pair is left to graze.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: The second goat of the first pair is offered. The second goat of the second pair grazes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives his ruling about the leftover goats: use the old survivor, and set aside the new extra goat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Second of the first pair' means the goat left over from the original pair after its partner died. רב says it is still fit to be used, so it is offered. The extra goat from the new pair is not needed, so it grazes until it gets a blemish (ירעה).

keyTerms.meaning: It is offered as a קרבן
It grazes until it gets a blemish, then is sold

steps.confusionAlert: 'שני' here does not mean 'the second goat in line.' It means 'the other goat,' the one left over in that pair.

phrases.english: Rav said:
The second one of the first pair is offered,
phrases.notes: The survivor of the original pair.

phrases.english: the second one of the second pair grazes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: שֵׁנִי שֶׁבְּזוּג רִאשׁוֹן — יִקְרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the משנה's case from step 4: which leftover goat is used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The survivor of the first pair is offered. The extra goat of the second pair grazes.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the leftover of the second pair is offered
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules the opposite of רב: the survivor of the first pair grazes, and the extra goat of the second pair is offered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The second goat of the first pair grazes. The second goat of the second pair is offered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב and flips the ruling. The old survivor is set aside, and the new goat is used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן holds that the old survivor was put aside for good when its partner died, so it is never used. That is why the goat from the new pair is offered instead. The גמרא explains the reason for each side in the next steps.
steps.whatToRemember: רב: the old survivor is offered, and the new extra goat grazes. רבי יוחנן: the old survivor grazes, and the new extra goat is offered.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
The second one of the first pair grazes,
the second one of the second pair is offered.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: שֵׁנִי שֶׁבְּזוּג רִאשׁוֹן — יִרְעֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite opinion to רב in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The survivor of the first pair grazes. The extra goat of the second pair is offered.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle lies underneath the argument between רב and רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what deeper idea makes רב and רבי יוחנן rule in opposite ways. It is setting up the next move, where it will name that idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5 and 6 told us only the rulings: which goat is offered and which one grazes. Now the גמרא wants the reason behind those rulings, so it asks for the general principle they argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: About what do they disagree? (asks for the root principle of an argument)

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the principle underneath the two opposite rulings of רב and רבי יוחנן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides רב and רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Can a live animal be permanently rejected?
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that בעלי חיים אינן נדחין. רבי יוחנן holds that בעלי חיים נדחין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב holds that live animals are not permanently rejected. רבי יוחנן holds that live animals are permanently rejected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names the principle. רב says a live animal that became unfit can become fit again. רבי יוחנן says once it was pushed off, it stays pushed off forever.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When its partner died, the surviving goat could not be used, so it was 'pushed off.' According to רב that rejection is not permanent, so once a new pair is brought, the survivor is offered. According to רבי יוחנן the rejection is permanent, so the survivor can only graze.

keyTerms.meaning: Are pushed off, meaning permanently rejected from being offered

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of דיחוי (permanent rejection) for live animals is a major principle that comes up across קדשים. This argument is the foundation for the rest of the סוגיא.
steps.confusionAlert: נדחה does not mean the goat stops being holy. It stays קדוש. The question is only whether it can still be offered on the מזבח. That is why under רבי יוחנן it grazes instead of being used for anything else.

phrases.aramaic: רַב סָבַר: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָן נִידְחִין,
phrases.english: Rav holds: live animals are not rejected,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִידְחִין.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yochanan holds: live animals are rejected.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סָבַר: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָן נִידְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by naming the principle.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The argument is whether בעלי חיים נדחין: רב says no, רבי יוחנן says yes.

steps.title: What is the source of רב's view?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind רב's position that live animals are not rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רב gets his idea that a live animal is never permanently rejected. It is setting up an attempt to find a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that we know רב's principle, the גמרא wants to know what it is based on. It will look for a similar case in הלכה from which רב could learn.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Rav?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רב's principle stated in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or comparison from which רב learns that בעלי חיים אינן נדחין.

steps.title: First suggestion: רב learns from an animal too young to be offered
steps.stepSummary: רב learns from מחוסר זמן, an animal that cannot be offered now but becomes fit later.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from an animal that is 'lacking time.' With such an animal, even though it is unfit now, isn't it fine once it becomes fit? Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that רב compares the goat to a מחוסר זמן, an animal too young to be brought as a קרבן yet. Such an animal is unfit now but becomes fine later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחוסר זמן (for example, an animal under eight days old) can't be offered now, but once it is old enough it is offered with no problem. The suggestion is that the surviving goat is the same: unfit for now, but fine once a new pair is brought.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal 'lacking time,' too young to be offered yet

phrases.english: He learns it from an animal lacking time.
An animal lacking time, is it not so

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּהַשְׁתָּא לָא חֲזֵי,
phrases.english: that even though now it is not fit,
when it later becomes fit, it is fine?
Here too, it is no different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to step 9's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב compares the case to מחוסר זמן: temporarily unfit animals become fit later.

steps.title: The comparison fails: a young animal was never fit at all
steps.stepSummary: A מחוסר זמן was never fit, but our goat was fit and then pushed off, so the cases are not alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it comparable? There, it was never fit at all. Here, it was fit and then was pushed off!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the comparison to מחוסר זמן. It points out an important difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מחוסר זמן was never fit in the first place, so there was nothing to reject. The goat in our case was fit, and then became unfit when its partner died. Perhaps 'fit and then pushed off' (נראה ונדחה) is exactly what makes something permanently rejected, so מחוסר זמן proves nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: It was fit and then was pushed off

phrases.english: Is it comparable?
There, it was never fit at all.
Here, it was fit and then rejected!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי דָּמֵי? הָתָם לָא אִיתְחֲזִי כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the מחוסר זמן comparison, not רב's position itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: מחוסר זמן was never fit, while the goat was fit and then rejected (נראה ונדחה). Only that second situation creates real דיחוי.

steps.title: Second suggestion: רב learns from an animal with a temporary blemish
steps.stepSummary: רב learns from בעל מום עובר, an animal that was fit, became blemished, and becomes fit again once it heals.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason of רב: he learns it from an animal with a temporary blemish. With such an animal, even though it is unfit now, isn't it fine once it becomes fit again? Here too, it is no different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the first comparison and offers a better one: an animal with a temporary blemish. Like our goat, it was fit, became unfit, and later becomes fit again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This comparison answers the problem from step 11. A בעל מום עובר was fit, became unfit (just like נראה ונדחה), and yet is offered once the blemish heals. This shows that a live animal that was fit and then pushed off can return, which is exactly רב's view.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal with a temporary, passing blemish
Rather (drops the earlier answer and gives a new one)

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason of Rav:
he learns it from an animal with a temporary blemish.
An animal with a temporary blemish, is it not so

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא חֲזֵי הַשְׁתָּא,
phrases.english: that even though it is not fit now,
when it later becomes fit, it is fine?
Here too, it is no different.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַב, דְּיָלֵיף מִבַּעַל מוּם עוֹבֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected מחוסר זמן source with a בעל מום עובר source that avoids the problem raised in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב learns from בעל מום עובר, which was fit, became unfit, and returns to being fit.

steps.title: How do we know the temporary-blemish rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a בעל מום עובר can be offered after it heals.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks how we know that an animal with a temporary blemish is fine once it heals. It is setting up a פסוק as the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's whole proof depends on the rule of בעל מום עובר. So the גמרא makes sure that rule itself has a firm source.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the בעל מום עובר rule that רב relies on in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a temporarily blemished animal becomes fit once it heals.

steps.title: The פסוק: only while the blemish is in them are they rejected
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'מום בם' teaches that only while the blemish is present are they not accepted. Once it passes, they are accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'Because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them.' While the blemish is in them, they are not accepted. But once their blemish passes, they are accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a פסוק in ויקרא to prove the rule of a temporary blemish. The words 'מום בם' (a blemish is in them) limit the disqualification to the time the blemish is actually there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words 'מום בם' teach that the problem is only while the blemish is present. Once it heals, the animal is accepted. This means a live animal that was fit and then rejected can become fit again, which completes the support for רב's view that בעלי חיים אינן נדחין.

keyTerms.meaning: They will be accepted (as a קרבן)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: בעלי חיים אינן נדחין, learned from בעל מום עובר (based on 'מום בם'), not from מחוסר זמן, because מחוסר זמן was never fit. רבי יוחנן: בעלי חיים נדחין.

phrases.english: As it is written: "Because their corruption is in them, there is a blemish in them,"
while the blemish is in them, they will not be accepted;
but if their blemish passed, they will be accepted.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: כִּי מׇשְׁחָתָם בָּהֶם מוּם בָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 with a פסוק, securing the בעל מום עובר source for רב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא כב:כה, 'מום בם': the disqualification lasts only while the blemish is present.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן limits the blemish rule to blemished animals only
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers רב's proof: the word 'בהם' limits the 'comes back to fitness' rule to blemished animals. All other rejected animals stay rejected.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would רבי יוחנן respond? The Torah limited this with the word 'בהם' ('in them'). Only blemished animals become accepted again when their blemish passes. All other animals that were pushed off, once they are pushed off, stay pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן deals with רב's proof from a בעל מום עובר. It answers that the פסוק itself limits that rule to blemished animals only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב had argued: a blemished animal was fit, got pushed off, and becomes fit again, so our goat should work the same way. רבי יוחנן says the word 'בהם' ('them') points to blemished animals specifically. That makes them a special exception, and you cannot build a general rule from them. So the general rule stays: הואיל ונדחו נדחו.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the Torah) limited / excluded
'In them': the word in the פסוק about blemished animals
They will be accepted (as a valid offering)
Since they were pushed off, they stay pushed off

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן agrees that a בעל מום עובר becomes fit again after it heals. He is not denying step 14. He only says this is a special exception that cannot be stretched to other rejected animals.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the core disagreement. For רבי יוחנן, being pushed off (דיחוי) is permanent except where the Torah says otherwise. רב will now have to show that 'בהם' is needed for a different lesson.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan? (How does he respond?)
The Merciful One limited it with "in them"
phrases.notes: The word from the פסוק quoted in step 14

phrases.aramaic: הֵם הוּא דְּכִי עָבַר מוּמָן יֵרָצוּ,
phrases.english: it is they who, when their blemish passes, are accepted
but all other pushed-off animals
since they were pushed off, they remain pushed off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב's proof from בעל מום עובר by reading the same פסוק as a limitation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using בעל מום עובר as a model for all pushed-off animals.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק's word 'בהם' marks blemished animals as a unique exception, so no general rule can be learned from them.

steps.title: רב reads 'in them' as being about mixtures
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that 'בהם' means blemished animals are not accepted on their own, but they are accepted inside a mixture.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how does רב respond? That word 'בהם' means: on their own, they are not accepted. But through mixtures, they are accepted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רב handles רבי יוחנן's reading. רב says the word 'בהם' teaches a different lesson, so it is not a limitation on his proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן used 'בהם' to block רב's proof. רב keeps his proof by giving 'בהם' another job. It teaches that blemished animals are rejected only 'in themselves' (בעינייהו), meaning when they stand alone. When they are mixed with fit animals (תערובות), they can be accepted. Since 'בהם' is used up on that lesson, it cannot serve as רבי יוחנן's limitation.

keyTerms.meaning: In their own state / on their own

phrases.english: And Rav? (How does he respond?)
That "in them" means: in their own state
is when they are not accepted
but through mixtures, they are accepted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רב against רבי יוחנן's reading by assigning 'בהם' a different lesson.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the דרשה: the word is needed for another הלכה, so it cannot serve as a limitation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'בהם' limits fitness-after-rejection to blemished animals only.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'בהם' teaches that blemished animals are rejected alone but accepted inside a mixture.

steps.title: משנה about mixed limbs supports רב's reading
steps.stepSummary: A משנה about unblemished and blemished limbs that got mixed: רבי אליעזר allows offering them, and חכמים require the leftover to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: limbs of unblemished animals got mixed with limbs of blemished animals. רבי אליעזר says: if the head of one of them was offered, all the heads should be offered. If the legs of one of them were offered, all the legs should be offered. חכמים say: even if all of them were offered except one, that last one must go out to the place of burning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for רב's idea that blemished items can be accepted inside a mixture. That source is the view of רבי אליעזר in a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats the mixture as acceptable. Once one head is offered, we assume it was the blemished one, so the rest may all be offered. This shows that blemished items can be 'accepted through mixture', matching רב's reading of 'בהם'. חכמים disagree and do not rely on that assumption. They require the last piece to be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The place where disqualified offerings are burned

steps.confusionAlert: The proof comes from רבי אליעזר's view only. חכמים disagree. The point is simply that there is a position that blemished items can be accepted in a mixture, which is what רב's reading of 'בהם' needs.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
Limbs of unblemished offerings that got mixed with limbs of blemished ones.
Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם קָרַב הָרֹאשׁ שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶן —
phrases.english: If the head of one of them was offered,
they should offer all the heads,
phrases.notes: We assume the blemished head was the one already offered.

phrases.english: if the legs of one of them were offered,
they should offer all the legs.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ קָרְבוּ כּוּלָּן חוּץ מֵאֶחָד מֵהֶן —
phrases.english: Even if all of them were offered except one,
it must go out to the place of burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן: אֵיבָרִים תְּמִימִים בְּאֵיבָרִים בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies a משנה source showing that blemished items can be accepted through a mixture, as רב said.
steps.raayaObject: The הלכה that blemished items are accepted through תערובות, which רב reads into 'בהם'.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of mixed limbs, according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן learns mixtures from 'בם' versus 'בהם'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also accepts the mixture law. He learns it from the longer spelling 'בהם' instead of 'בם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רבי יוחנן)? He learns it from 'בם' versus 'בהם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יוחנן gets the mixture law, since he used 'בהם' as a limitation. It answers that he learns it from the extra letter ה in the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah could have written the short form 'בם' but wrote 'בהם', with an extra ה. רבי יוחנן uses the word itself for his limitation and the extra letter for the mixture law. This way he gets both lessons from one word.

keyTerms.meaning: 'In them': the shorter spelling, without the extra ה

phrases.english: And the other (Rabbi Yochanan)? (Where does he learn mixtures?)
He derives it from "bam" versus "bahem".
phrases.notes: The Torah used the longer form, which adds an extra lesson.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how רבי יוחנן gets the mixture law that רב read into 'בהם'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבי יוחנן learns that blemished items are accepted through mixtures.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From the extra ה in 'בהם' instead of 'בם'.

steps.title: רב does not expound 'בם' versus 'בהם'
steps.stepSummary: רב does not learn anything from the spelling difference between 'בם' and 'בהם', so 'בהם' is fully used up on the mixture law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one (רב)? He does not expound 'בם' versus 'בהם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב cannot learn both lessons the way רבי יוחנן does. He simply does not derive anything from the spelling difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב, 'בם' and 'בהם' mean the same thing, so there is no extra letter to learn from. The word 'בהם' gives only one lesson, and he needs it for mixtures. That leaves no limitation, so רב's proof from בעל מום עובר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He does not expound (derive a law from it)

steps.whatToRemember: Both רב and רבי יוחנן agree on the mixture law. Their argument is over how many lessons 'בהם' can teach. For רבי יוחנן it teaches two (the limitation plus mixtures), so being pushed off stays permanent for everything else. For רב it teaches only mixtures, so the blemish case remains a valid proof that a pushed-off animal can become fit again.

phrases.english: And the other (Rav)?
He does not expound "bam" versus "bahem".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רב cannot adopt רבי יוחנן's double reading, which closes this exchange.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב does not also use the spelling difference, which would free 'בהם' to be a limitation.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב does not derive any law from the difference between 'בם' and 'בהם'.

steps.title: Why must רב use the first goat at all?
steps.stepSummary: Even if living animals are not rejected (בעלי חיים אינן נדחין), the כהן should be free to offer either the old goat or the new one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב: fine, living animals are not rejected. But then, if he wants he should offer this one, and if he wants he should offer that one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב. His rule only shows that the old goat is still allowed. It does not show that the old goat must be the one used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's principle that living animals are not rejected (בעלי חיים אינן נדחין) only makes the leftover goat of the first pair kosher. It does not explain why that goat gets priority over the matching goat from the new pair. So the גמרא asks why there is no free choice.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, even if we accept that
Living animals are not permanently rejected

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether the old goat is allowed. רב already said it is. The question is why it must be chosen over the new one.

phrases.english: And according to Rav,

phrases.aramaic: נְהִי נָמֵי דְּבַעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָן נִדְחִין,
phrases.english: granted that living animals are not rejected,
if he wants, let him offer this one,
if he wants, let him offer that one!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts רב's view that the old goat is not rejected, then asks a further question about why it gets priority.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the leftover goat of the first pair must be the one used
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not being rejected only makes the goat allowed. It does not make it required, so the כהן should have a free choice.

steps.title: רבא: רב follows רבי יוסי that the first one is preferred
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רב holds like רבי יוסי, who says the מצוה should be done with the first one (מצוה בראשון).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: רב holds like רבי יוסי, who said that the מצוה is with the first one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. רב follows a separate rule of רבי יוסי that the first animal set aside gets priority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The priority does not come from 'not rejected.' It comes from a second principle: מצוה בראשון. Since the first pair came first, its leftover goat should be the one used.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה is best done with the first one

steps.whyThisMatters: This adds a second idea alongside 'not rejected': priority of the first. The rest of the passage searches for where that idea comes from.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Rav holds like Rabbi Yosei,
who said: the מצוה is with the first one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: רַב סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings in an outside principle (מצוה בראשון) from another תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With no reason to prefer the first goat, the כהן could choose either one.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows רבי יוסי's rule of מצוה בראשון, so the first pair's goat comes first.

steps.title: Which statement of רבי יוסי is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which teaching of רבי יוסי shows that he holds מצוה בראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which רבי יוסי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יוסי says this rule. This sets up the next steps, which test possible sources.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says 'מצוה בראשון' in more than one place. The גמרא wants the source that truly matches the goat case.

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Yosei?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the principle רבא cited.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The specific teaching of רבי יוסי that establishes מצוה בראשון in a way that fits the goats

steps.title: First suggestion: רבי יוסי on the coin containers
steps.stepSummary: Perhaps the source is רבי יוסי's explanation of why the three לשכה containers were labeled א, ב, ג: to use the first-filled one first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is רבי יוסי of the containers: as we learned, there were three containers of three סאה each, with which they collected from the לשכה, and א, ב, ג was written on them. And a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי said, why was א, ב, ג written on them? To know which was filled first, in order to bring from it first, since the מצוה is with the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one possible source. It is רבי יוסי's teaching about the labeled coin containers in the לשכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The containers were labeled so that the money collected first would be spent first. רבי יוסי explains this with the words 'שמצוה בראשון,' which seems to be exactly רב's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking out the half-shekel coins from the Temple chamber

phrases.english: If you say it is Rabbi Yosei of the containers,
as we learned: three containers
of three se'ah each,
with which they collect from the chamber,
and written on them: alef, beit, gimmel.
And a baraita teaches: Rabbi Yosei said:

phrases.aramaic: לָמָּה כָּתוּב עֲלֵיהֶן אָלֶף בֵּית גִּימֶל —
phrases.english: Why is alef, beit, gimmel written on them?
To know which of them was filled first,
to bring (offerings) from it first,
for the מצוה is with the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first candidate answer to the question in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי holds מצוה בראשון, as רב needs
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה and ברייתא about the three labeled containers of the לשכה

steps.title: The containers case is different
steps.stepSummary: With the containers, the first one was ready before the later ones existed, so it naturally comes first. That does not prove anything about two goats that are both ready at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is different there, because at the time the first was fit, the later ones were not yet fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the containers as the source. The first container had priority only because it was ready earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the containers case, the first container could already be used while the others were not yet ready. With the goats, none of them can be offered until the proper point in the service, and by then both pairs are ready together. A rule that the first one wins when both are equally ready is not shown by the containers.

keyTerms.meaning: The first one / the later ones

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
for at the time the first one was fit,
the later ones were not yet fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the containers as the source suggested in Step 23.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the containers as a source. It does not reject רבי יוסי's principle itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the containers case, the first one was ready earlier. The goat case needs priority even when both are ready at the same time.

steps.title: The real source: רבי יוסי on the lost פסח
steps.stepSummary: The source is רבי יוסי's ruling about a lost קרבן פסח that was replaced and then found. Both animals are ready together, yet he says the first one should be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is רבי יוסי of the פסח. As we learned: one who set aside his פסח and it got lost, and he set aside another in its place, and afterward the first was found, and both are standing — he may offer whichever he wants; these are the words of the חכמים. רבי יוסי says: the מצוה is with the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct source for רב. It is רבי יוסי in the case of the lost and replaced פסח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both animals stand ready together, just like the two goats. The חכמים allow a free choice, which matches the challenge in Step 20. רבי יוסי says to use the first, which matches רב. So רב's view fits רבי יוסי's side of an argument with the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets aside an animal as his קרבן פסח

steps.whatToRemember: רב follows רבי יוסי: when two animals are both ready, the first one gets priority (מצוה בראשון). The source is the lost פסח case, not the containers, because only the פסח case has both animals ready at the same time.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רב's ruling sides with one view in an argument between תנאים. The חכמים would allow a free choice.

phrases.english: Rather, it is Rabbi Yosei of the Pesach,
(as we learned:) one who set aside his Pesach and it was lost,
and he set aside another in its place,
and afterward the first one was found,
and now both are standing —
whichever of them he wants may be offered,
these are the words of the Sages.
Rabbi Yosei says: the מצוה is with the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the containers in Step 24, it gives the correct source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is רבי יוסי's ruling about the lost פסח, where both animals are ready together and he still says the first should be used.
